providers.action.install.description: Provider Setup's button: installs the coding agent's CLI in a terminal.

providers.action.signIn.description: Provider Setup's button: signs the coding agent's CLI in, in a terminal.

providers.action.update.description: Provider Setup's button: updates the coding agent's CLI in a terminal.

providers.antigravity.checkFailed.defaultMessage: Couldn't check {provider}'s sign-in: {text}. Choose Check again; if you haven't signed in yet, run agy in a terminal.
providers.antigravity.checkFailed.description: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI, when listing its models failed for a reason other than a known sign-in error (a network or service error, a timeout). {provider} is its name, {text} the CLI's own words (not translated). agy is a command: keep it; Check again is a button.

providers.antigravity.conversationGone.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't resume {conversation}: {provider} no longer has that conversation (it keeps it apart from its transcript, in the agent's profile, and it was removed). Start a new session instead.
providers.antigravity.conversationGone.description: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't resume a conversation (its pane): the conversation's own store in the agent's profile is gone, though its transcript may be left. {provider} is the CLI's name, {conversation} the conversation's id.

providers.antigravity.guidanceTooLong.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: Combwork's guidance, this agent's instructions and the Workspace notes come to {size, number} bytes, and {provider} reads at most {max, number} bytes of its rules file, cutting off the rest. Shorten the agent's instructions (Agent Settings) or the Workspace notes, then start the agent again.
providers.antigravity.guidanceTooLong.description: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't start (its pane): what Combwork gives it as its rules file is over Antigravity's size limit, which would cut it off. {provider} is the CLI's name, {size} and {max} sizes in bytes. Agent Settings and Workspace notes are places in Combwork: keep them.

providers.antigravity.notOwnConversation.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't resume {conversation}: it isn't in this agent's own conversations (it may have been removed, or be another agent's). Start a new session instead.
providers.antigravity.notOwnConversation.description: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't resume a conversation (its pane): the conversation isn't among this agent's own. {provider} is the CLI's name, {conversation} the conversation's id.

providers.antigravity.notice.auto.defaultMessage: Auto runs commands inside Antigravity’s own sandbox, which needs Windows 11 24H2 or later with the August 2026 update or later. This PC runs Windows build {version}, so Antigravity may refuse Auto or ask before commands. Choose another mode in Agent Settings, or update Windows.
providers.antigravity.notice.auto.description: Part of a notice as an Antigravity CLI agent starts in Auto mode on a Windows that can't run its sandbox (older than 11 24H2 with the August 2026 update). {version}: the Windows build and revision, such as 26100.8000. Auto is a permission mode, Agent Settings a place in Combwork: keep them; Windows 11 24H2 is a version.

providers.antigravity.notice.autoUnknown.defaultMessage: Auto runs commands inside Antigravity’s own sandbox, which needs Windows 11 24H2 or later with the August 2026 update or later. Combwork couldn’t read this PC’s Windows version, so it can’t tell whether Auto applies here: if Antigravity refuses Auto or asks before commands, choose another mode in Agent Settings, or update Windows.
providers.antigravity.notice.autoUnknown.description: Part of a notice as an Antigravity CLI agent starts in Auto mode where Combwork couldn't read the Windows version, so it can't tell whether Antigravity's sandbox applies. Auto is a permission mode, Agent Settings a place in Combwork: keep them; Windows 11 24H2 is a version.

providers.antigravity.notice.setup.defaultMessage: Antigravity isn’t set up yet, so this agent shows its first-run screens (a colour scheme, its terms) in its pane: complete them there, or once for every agent with Set up in Provider Setup.
providers.antigravity.notice.setup.description: Part of a notice as an Antigravity CLI agent starts before the user completed Antigravity's first-run screens in Provider Setup. Set up and Provider Setup are Combwork's names: keep them.

providers.antigravity.notice.sse.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {The MCP server {servers} uses} other {The MCP servers {servers} use}} the legacy HTTP+SSE transport, which Antigravity doesn’t support, so this agent runs without {count, plural, one {it} other {them}}. Change {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} to Streamable HTTP in MCP servers to use {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} here.
providers.antigravity.notice.sse.description: Part of a notice as an Antigravity CLI agent starts: MCP servers it was given use a transport Antigravity can't use, so they're left out. {servers}: their names joined as a list; {count}: how many. HTTP+SSE and Streamable HTTP are transports' names, MCP servers a place in Combwork: keep them.

providers.antigravity.notice.title.defaultMessage: Antigravity can’t use everything this agent was given
providers.antigravity.notice.title.description: A notice as an Antigravity CLI agent starts: something it was given can't apply (an MCP server's transport, a permission mode on this Windows).

providers.antigravity.projectServers.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: {count, plural, one {{files} defines} other {{files} define}} MCP servers this agent wasn't given ({servers}), and {provider} would start them in its session. Combwork can't keep them out, so it doesn't start {provider} here. Remove them from that file, or give them to the agent in Combwork's MCP servers.
providers.antigravity.projectServers.description: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't start (its pane): a project or added folder's .agents config defines MCP servers the agent wasn't given, which Antigravity can't be kept from starting. {provider} is the CLI's name, {files} the config files' paths joined as a list, {count} how many files, {servers} the servers' names joined as a list. MCP servers is a place in Combwork.

providers.antigravity.setup.action.description: Provider Setup's button: opens Antigravity CLI's first-run screens in a terminal.

providers.antigravity.setup.copied.defaultMessage: Each Antigravity agent then starts past those screens: Combwork copies only that they are done into its private profile, never your own Antigravity settings.
providers.antigravity.setup.copied.description: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI's Set up: what Combwork does with it.

providers.antigravity.setup.needed.defaultMessage: Antigravity needs a one-time setup: its first-run screens. Until then each new agent shows them in its pane.
providers.antigravity.setup.needed.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Antigravity CLI's first-run screens (a colour scheme, its terms of service) aren't done yet.

providers.antigravity.setup.runs.defaultMessage: **Set up** runs `agy` in a terminal: choose a colour scheme and read and accept its terms there, its data-use choice yours. Combwork types nothing into it, and closes it once you are done.
providers.antigravity.setup.runs.description: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI's Set up: what it does. **…** marks bold text and `…` a command: keep the marks and the command.

providers.antigravity.signIn.runs.defaultMessage: **Sign in** runs `agy` in a terminal: sign in there. Combwork never signs in for you.
providers.antigravity.signIn.runs.description: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI's Sign in: what it does. **…** marks bold text and `…` a command: keep the marks and the command.

providers.antigravity.signIn.shared.defaultMessage: The sign-in is this PC’s: every workspace’s Antigravity agents use it, and signing out signs them all out.
providers.antigravity.signIn.shared.description: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI's Sign in: its sign-in is shared by every workspace on this PC.

providers.antigravity.unreadableConfig.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: Combwork couldn't read {file} ({why}), which it would load. Fix or remove the file, then start the agent again.
providers.antigravity.unreadableConfig.description: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't start (its pane): a config file in the project (an MCP server or hook list) couldn't be read, so Combwork couldn't keep what it holds out of the agent. {provider} is the CLI's name, {file} a path, {why} the error's own words.

providers.autoCompact.autoIn.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file sets it to auto. {key} is the setting as written (autoCompactWindow), {scope} the file. "auto" is its value: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.badSources.defaultMessage: isn't a list Claude Code takes (user, project, local)
providers.autoCompact.badSources.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: --setting-sources (a command-line option, before this) has a value Claude Code doesn't take. user, project and local are its values: keep them.

providers.autoCompact.disabledIn.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file turns it off. autoCompactEnabled: false is the setting as written: keep it. {scope} is the file.

providers.autoCompact.envIn.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: an environment variable set in a settings file's env block. {variable} is its name, {scope} the file. env is the block's name: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.estimate.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: it is an estimate, in brackets after the window. {unsure} lists why, clauses joined as a list ("managed policies Combwork can't read … could change it and Claude Code's settings.json couldn't be read (EACCES)").

providers.autoCompact.keyIn.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file sets it. {key} is the setting as written (autoCompactWindow), {scope} the file.

providers.autoCompact.scope.local.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads, after "in" ({scope} in providers.autoCompact.keyIn, autoIn, disabledIn and envIn). .claude/settings.local.json is a path: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.scope.managed.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads, after "in" ({scope} in providers.autoCompact.keyIn, autoIn, disabledIn and envIn). The managed settings an administrator gives Claude Code.

providers.autoCompact.scope.project.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads, after "in" ({scope} in providers.autoCompact.keyIn, autoIn, disabledIn and envIn). .claude/settings.json is a path: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.scope.user.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads, after "in" ({scope} in providers.autoCompact.keyIn, autoIn, disabledIn and envIn). The user's own settings file. settings.json is a file name: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.unreadReason.defaultMessage: managed policies Combwork can't read (such as Windows registry policies or your organisation's server-managed settings) could change it
providers.autoCompact.unreadReason.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: why its default is an estimate. A clause, in a list of such reasons (providers.autoCompact.estimate).

providers.autoCompact.unreadable.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Combwork couldn't read (after its name). {why} says why (providers.autoCompact.why.*, or the system's message).

providers.autoCompact.unsureFile.local.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads that Combwork can't be sure of, a clause ("the project's .claude/settings.local.json couldn't be read (EACCES)"). {unsure} says why (providers.autoCompact.unreadable). .claude/settings.local.json is a path: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.unsureFile.managed.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads that Combwork can't be sure of, a clause ("managed settings couldn't be read (EACCES)"). {unsure} says why (providers.autoCompact.unreadable). The managed settings an administrator gives Claude Code.

providers.autoCompact.unsureFile.project.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads that Combwork can't be sure of, a clause ("the project's .claude/settings.json couldn't be read (EACCES)"). {unsure} says why (providers.autoCompact.unreadable). .claude/settings.json is a path: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.unsureFile.user.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a settings file Claude Code reads that Combwork can't be sure of, a clause ("Claude Code's settings.json couldn't be read (EACCES)"). {unsure} says why (providers.autoCompact.unreadable). The user's own settings file. settings.json is a file name: keep it.

providers.autoCompact.unsureMode.defaultMessage: may stop Claude Code reading some settings files
providers.autoCompact.unsureMode.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: a command-line option (before this: --safe-mode, --bare) may change which settings files Claude Code reads.

providers.autoCompact.unsureScope.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: settings Combwork can't be sure of, a clause. {scope} is a command-line option as typed, the clause's subject (--settings file.json, --setting-sources bogus, --safe-mode), {unsure} says why (couldn't be read…, providers.autoCompact.badSources, unsureMode).

providers.autoCompact.why.notFile.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: why Combwork couldn't read a settings file (providers.autoCompact.unreadable).

providers.autoCompact.why.tooBig.defaultMessage: it's over Claude Code's 2 MiB limit
providers.autoCompact.why.tooBig.description: Where Claude Code's auto-compaction setting comes from, in the context tooltip of an agent's footer: why Combwork couldn't read a settings file (providers.autoCompact.unreadable). 2 MiB is the size limit: keep it.

providers.claude.connections.setUp.defaultMessage: Set Up runs Claude Code on this connection for its one-time first-run questions (its look, its notes) and to trust this workspace's folders. Answer them in the terminal.
providers.claude.connections.setUp.description: Settings → Accounts & Connections, above a Claude Code connection's Set Up terminal and on one that still needs it: what Set Up is for. Set Up names a button.

providers.claude.hint.args.defaultMessage: Claude Code refused an argument: check Extra arguments in Agent Settings and Settings → Claude Code.
providers.claude.hint.args.description: Why Claude Code didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.claude.hint.broken.defaultMessage: Claude Code looks broken or missing: reinstall or update it in Provider Setup.
providers.claude.hint.broken.description: Why Claude Code didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.claude.hint.model.defaultMessage: Claude Code doesn't know this model: choose another in Agent Settings.
providers.claude.hint.model.description: Why Claude Code didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.claude.hint.signIn.defaultMessage: Claude Code isn't signed in: start it again and sign in in its terminal.
providers.claude.hint.signIn.description: Why Claude Code didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.claude.localLimits.inFile.description: Where a local model's limit came from (HI-2682): a Claude Code settings file's env block. {file} names the file. env is the block's name: keep it.

providers.claude.localLimits.oursContext.description: Where a local model's context came from (HI-2682), in an error or a tooltip: the server connection's model field. {connection} is the connection's name. Context size is the field's name: as translated there.

providers.claude.localLimits.oursOutput.description: Where a local model's output budget came from (HI-2682), in an error or a tooltip: the server connection's model field, or its default. {connection} is the connection's name. Output budget is the field's name: as translated there.

providers.claude.localLimits.outputNotBe.defaultMessage: {agent} wasn’t started: its output budget ({output, number} tokens, {outputFrom}) isn’t below its context size ({context, number} tokens, {contextFrom}). Change one of them, then start it again.
providers.claude.localLimits.outputNotBe.description: An error starting an agent on a local model (HI-2682): the output budget Claude Code would get isn't smaller than its context. {agent} is the agent's name; {output} and {context} are numbers of tokens; {outputFrom} and {contextFrom} say where each was set ("Context size on Local", "env in the project's .claude/settings.json").

providers.claude.localLimits.tooSmall.defaultMessage: {agent} wasn’t started: its context size ({context, number} tokens, {contextFrom}) is too small for any output budget. Set a larger context size.
providers.claude.localLimits.tooSmall.description: An error starting an agent on a local model (HI-2682): its context is so small that no output budget fits. {agent} is the agent's name; {context} is a number of tokens; {contextFrom} says where it was set.

providers.claude.policy.file.description: Where a Claude Code setting that blocks Combwork's hooks was found: the managed-settings.json an administrator gives Claude Code (C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode). Used after "in" or as a subject in the hooks warning.

providers.claude.policy.hkcu.defaultMessage: your Claude Code policy in the registry (HKCU)
providers.claude.policy.hkcu.description: Where a Claude Code setting that blocks Combwork's hooks was found: a policy in the Windows registry for the current user. Used after "in" or as a subject in the hooks warning. Keep HKCU.

providers.claude.policy.hklm.defaultMessage: the computer's Claude Code policy in the registry (HKLM)
providers.claude.policy.hklm.description: Where a Claude Code setting that blocks Combwork's hooks was found: a policy in the Windows registry for the whole computer. Used after "in" or as a subject in the hooks warning. Keep HKLM.

providers.cmdTooLong.defaultMessage: {file} has to run through cmd.exe, which takes a command line of at most {max, number} characters, and this launch needs about {length, number}. Set the CLI's path in Settings to its .exe (or install the standalone CLI), which has no such limit.
providers.cmdTooLong.description: Starting an agent is refused: its CLI is a .cmd or .bat launcher, and cmd.exe can't take a command line this long. {file} is the launcher's file name; {max} and {length} are numbers of characters. Keep cmd.exe and .exe as they are.

providers.codex.connections.setUp.defaultMessage: Set Up runs Codex on this connection so you can choose its Windows sandbox, which its commands run in, and trust this workspace's folders. Answer in the terminal; Windows may ask for Administrator permission.
providers.codex.connections.setUp.description: Settings → Accounts & Connections, above a Codex connection's Set Up terminal and on one that still needs it: what Set Up is for. Set Up names a button.

providers.codex.developerUnread.agentMes.defaultMessage: Codex couldn't say which developer_instructions this session gets, so Combwork leaves yours as they are and adds none of its guidance this time: the agent has Combwork's tools without it. Restart the agent to try again.
providers.codex.developerUnread.agentMes.description: The notice that a Codex agent started without Combwork's guidance. developer_instructions is a Codex setting: keep it.

providers.codex.developerUnread.agentTit.defaultMessage: Combwork's guidance is missing for this agent
providers.codex.developerUnread.agentTit.description: A notice as a Codex agent starts: Combwork couldn't tell which of the user's own Codex instructions apply, so it added none of its guidance.

providers.codex.developerUnread.assistan.defaultMessage: Codex couldn't say which developer_instructions this session gets, so Combwork gives the Assistant its role alone this time, without them or Combwork's guidance. Restart the Assistant to try again.
providers.codex.developerUnread.assistan.description: The notice that the Combwork Assistant on Codex got only its role. developer_instructions is a Codex setting: keep it.

providers.codex.developerUnread.assistan.defaultMessage: The Assistant started with its role only
providers.codex.developerUnread.assistan.description: A notice as the Combwork Assistant starts on Codex: Combwork couldn't tell which of the user's own Codex instructions apply, so it gives the Assistant only its role.

providers.codex.hint.broken.defaultMessage: Codex looks broken or not set up: check it in Provider Setup.
providers.codex.hint.broken.description: Why Codex didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.codex.hint.model.defaultMessage: Codex doesn't know this model: choose another in Agent Settings.
providers.codex.hint.model.description: Why Codex didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.codex.hint.settings.defaultMessage: Codex refused its settings: check Extra arguments in Agent Settings and Settings → Codex, and your config.toml.
providers.codex.hint.settings.description: Why Codex didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.codex.hint.signIn.defaultMessage: Codex isn't signed in: sign in in Provider Setup, then start it again.
providers.codex.hint.signIn.description: Why Codex didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.codex.nativeCombwork.defaultMessage: Your Codex config has an MCP server named combwork, reached over HTTP ({file}). Codex merges it into Combwork’s own combwork server, and can’t start with both. Rename yours there to start Codex agents.
providers.codex.nativeCombwork.description: Why a Codex agent didn't start: the user's own Codex config has an MCP server named combwork. {file} is that config file's path. combwork is the name of Combwork's MCP server (HI-2463): keep it.

providers.codex.sandbox.default.defaultMessage: **Set up default sandbox** (recommended): commands run under two local Windows accounts Codex creates for them (`CodexSandboxOffline` and `CodexSandboxOnline`), with a firewall rule that keeps them offline unless you allow it. It isolates commands best. Windows asks for Administrator permission once.
providers.codex.sandbox.default.description: Provider Setup, under Codex's sandbox setup (Windows): its first choice. **Set up default sandbox** is the choice as Codex names it (in English); `…` marks account names: keep them.

providers.codex.sandbox.needed.defaultMessage: Codex needs a one-time setup of its Windows sandbox; until then it asks before every command.
providers.codex.sandbox.needed.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Codex's Windows sandbox isn't set up yet.

providers.codex.sandbox.nonAdmin.defaultMessage: **Use non-admin sandbox**: needs no Administrator permission. Commands run under your own account with restricted rights. It protects your files and blocks internet access in most cases, but Codex warns it carries more risk if the agent is tricked by instructions hidden in a file or web page it reads (prompt injection). You can upgrade to the default sandbox from here later.
providers.codex.sandbox.nonAdmin.description: Provider Setup, under Codex's sandbox setup (Windows): its second choice. **Use non-admin sandbox** is the choice as Codex names it (in English).

providers.codex.sandbox.nonAdminUsed.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Codex runs commands in its non-admin sandbox (Windows), which can be upgraded.

providers.codex.sandbox.setUp.defaultMessage: **Set up** opens Codex's sandbox setup, which offers two choices. With either, Codex agents in **Ask for approval** or **Approve for me** can edit files in their own folder (the project, or the agent's worktree) and run commands there without asking, and ask before going online or writing anywhere else. Combwork's own features (status, file locks, handovers, shared notes) work the same with both.
providers.codex.sandbox.setUp.description: Provider Setup, under Codex's sandbox setup (Windows): what Set up does. **…** marks bold text: keep the marks. Set up is the button; Ask for approval and Approve for me are Codex's permission modes as Combwork names them: use their names as shown.

providers.codex.sandbox.setUpAction.description: Provider Setup's button: opens Codex's sandbox setup in a terminal.

providers.codex.sandbox.upgrade.defaultMessage: **Upgrade** switches Codex to its default sandbox, which runs commands under separate Windows accounts instead of your own. Windows asks for Administrator permission once. Codex agents that are running keep their sandbox until they restart.
providers.codex.sandbox.upgrade.description: Provider Setup, under Codex's sandbox setup (Windows): what Upgrade does. **…** marks bold text: keep the marks.

providers.codex.sandbox.upgradeAction.description: Provider Setup's button: switches Codex to its default sandbox.

providers.codex.storePwsh.fix.defaultMessage: To avoid it, replace the Store's PowerShell 7 with the installer's, in this order. First uninstall the Store one (Settings → Apps → Installed apps → PowerShell → Uninstall, or `Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell | Remove-AppxPackage`): while it is there, winget takes it for the same app and installs nothing. Then install PowerShell 7 (`winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget --installer-type wix`). Then restart Combwork and its Codex agents: they keep their old PATH until they restart. Combwork leaves your shell as it is.
providers.codex.storePwsh.fix.description: Provider Setup (#585, #1512), under the warning about the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7: what to do, in an order that must stay (uninstall the Store copy first, then install, then restart). `…` marks a command to type: keep it as it is. Settings → Apps → Installed apps is Windows 11's settings page: use Windows' own names for it in your language.

providers.codex.storePwsh.label.defaultMessage: PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is installed
providers.codex.storePwsh.label.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers (#585, #1404): the short label of the warning about the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7 (a badge and the banner atop the window); the explanation follows under it.

providers.codex.storePwsh.symptom.defaultMessage: The symptom: a Codex command fails at once with `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5` (access denied), and works again once every PowerShell 7 window and command is closed.
providers.codex.storePwsh.symptom.description: Provider Setup (#585), under the warning about the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7: how the problem shows. `…` marks the error as Codex prints it: keep it as it is.

providers.codex.storePwsh.warning.defaultMessage: Codex agents' commands can fail while a PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is open: Codex's Windows sandbox can't start that PowerShell while another copy of it runs.
providers.codex.storePwsh.warning.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers (#585): a warning that Codex's commands fail (Windows) while the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7, the one found first, is running anywhere, e.g. in a terminal. Codex is the coding agent's name.

providers.codex.stray.message.defaultMessage: {folder} holds {files}, which isn't Codex configuration (config.toml, agents, rules) or a file it names. Codex treats the folder as its own, and stray files in it (an agent's scratch or logs) can make every Codex agent's commands fail ("setup refresh had errors"). Move those files out of it (scratch belongs outside the project); leave Codex's configuration where it is.
providers.codex.stray.message.description: The warning about a stray .codex folder. {folder} is its path, {files} what it holds. config.toml, agents and rules are Codex's own names; "setup refresh had errors" is Codex's message, in English: keep them.

providers.codex.stray.more.description: The last item of the files a stray .codex folder holds, in its warning (providers.codex.stray.message), after the first few: how many more files there are. Combwork joins it to the list ("a.log, b.log, c.log and 2 more").

providers.codex.stray.title.defaultMessage: A .codex folder here can stop Codex running commands
providers.codex.stray.title.description: A warning when an agent starts in a folder with a .codex folder that isn't Codex's configuration. .codex is a folder's name.

providers.copilot.hint.args.defaultMessage: Copilot refused an argument: check Extra arguments in Agent Settings and Settings → GitHub Copilot.
providers.copilot.hint.args.description: Why GitHub Copilot didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.copilot.hint.broken.defaultMessage: Copilot looks broken or missing: check it in Provider Setup.
providers.copilot.hint.broken.description: Why GitHub Copilot didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.copilot.hint.mcp.defaultMessage: Copilot couldn't read the MCP configuration Combwork gave it: start it again.
providers.copilot.hint.mcp.description: Why GitHub Copilot didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.copilot.hint.model.defaultMessage: Copilot doesn't offer this model to this account (Copilot Free runs Auto only): choose another in Agent Settings.
providers.copilot.hint.model.description: Why GitHub Copilot didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.copilot.hint.signIn.defaultMessage: Copilot isn't signed in: sign in as Provider Setup shows, then start it again.
providers.copilot.hint.signIn.description: Why GitHub Copilot didn't start, in the agent's pane, with a button that goes where it says. Agent Settings, Provider Setup and Settings → … are Combwork's names: use them as shown.

providers.copilot.host.choose.defaultMessage: {repoHost} is a GitHub Enterprise Server host: choose where Copilot signs in (github.com or your GHE.com host) in Version Control → GitHub. Its Copilot agents don’t start until you do.
providers.copilot.host.choose.description: Provider Setup, GitHub Copilot (HI-2779): a project’s repositories are on a GitHub Enterprise Server host ({repoHost}), where cloud Copilot can’t sign in, and no Copilot host was chosen. Version Control → GitHub names the setting’s place. GHE.com is GitHub’s product name.

providers.copilot.host.deviceCode.defaultMessage: For a code to enter instead, run `copilot login --host {host} --device-code` in a terminal.
providers.copilot.host.deviceCode.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot’s Sign in for a GitHub host (HI-2779): another way to sign in. {host} is the host. `…` marks a command: keep it.

providers.copilot.host.gh.defaultMessage: With no login of its own there, Copilot uses the GitHub CLI’s login on {host} (`gh auth login --hostname {host}`), never one on another host.
providers.copilot.host.gh.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot’s Sign in for a GitHub host (HI-2779): Copilot falls back to the GitHub CLI’s sign-in on the same host only. {host} is the host. `…` marks a command: keep it.

providers.copilot.host.proxy.defaultMessage: GitHub Enterprise Server’s Copilot proxy is a preview Combwork doesn’t support yet: choose github.com or your GHE.com host in Version Control → GitHub. Its Copilot agents don’t start until you do.
providers.copilot.host.proxy.description: Provider Setup, GitHub Copilot (HI-2779): the Copilot sign-in setting chose GitHub Enterprise Server’s Copilot proxy (a GitHub preview), not supported yet. Version Control → GitHub names the setting’s place. GHE.com is GitHub’s product name.

providers.copilot.host.signInRuns.defaultMessage: **Sign in** runs `copilot login --host {host}` in a terminal: it opens {host} in your browser to authorise Copilot. Combwork never signs in for you.
providers.copilot.host.signInRuns.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot's Sign in for a GitHub host other than github.com (HI-2779): what it does. {host} is the host. **…** marks bold text and `…` a command: keep the marks and the command.

providers.copilot.host.signedOut.description: Provider Setup, GitHub Copilot (HI-2779): no sign-in found for a GitHub host Combwork’s projects use. {host} is the host (github.com, yourcompany.ghe.com).

providers.copilot.parens.message.defaultMessage: Copilot can't approve edits in a folder whose path has parentheses, so this agent asks before each edit, as in Ask. Rename the folder to give it Accept edits.
providers.copilot.parens.message.description: The notice that a GitHub Copilot agent asks before each edit. Ask and Accept edits are permission modes as Combwork names them: use their names as shown.

providers.copilot.parens.title.defaultMessage: Copilot will ask before each edit
providers.copilot.parens.title.description: A notice as a GitHub Copilot agent starts in Accept edits, in a folder whose path has parentheses.

providers.copilot.planNote.defaultMessage: Copilot Free uses Auto only; choosing a model needs a paid plan.
providers.copilot.planNote.description: A note in Provider Setup under GitHub Copilot. Copilot Free is the plan's name; Auto is Copilot's model choice: keep both names.

providers.copilot.signIn.deviceCode.defaultMessage: For a code to enter on GitHub instead, run `copilot login --device-code` in a terminal.
providers.copilot.signIn.deviceCode.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot's Sign in: another way to sign in. `…` marks a command: keep it.

providers.copilot.signIn.gh.defaultMessage: With no login of its own, Copilot uses the GitHub CLI’s (`gh auth login`).
providers.copilot.signIn.gh.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot's Sign in: Copilot falls back to the GitHub CLI's sign-in. `…` marks a command: keep it.

providers.copilot.signIn.ignored.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {Copilot agents don’t get {variables} from Combwork’s environment, so it doesn’t sign them in. For a token of Copilot’s own, set `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`.} other {Copilot agents don’t get {variables} from Combwork’s environment, so they don’t sign them in. For a token of Copilot’s own, set `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`.}}
providers.copilot.signIn.ignored.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot's Sign in: environment variables with a GitHub token that Combwork keeps from Copilot agents. {variables} lists them (joined with “or”), {n} is how many. `…` marks a variable name: keep it.

providers.copilot.signIn.runs.defaultMessage: **Sign in** runs `copilot login` in a terminal: it opens GitHub in your browser to authorise Copilot. Combwork never signs in for you.
providers.copilot.signIn.runs.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot's Sign in: what it does. **…** marks bold text and `…` a command: keep the marks and the command.

providers.copilot.signIn.switch.defaultMessage: Settings → Advanced → GitHub Copilot → **Keep GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN from Copilot** decides this, for every workspace.
providers.copilot.signIn.switch.description: Provider Setup, under GitHub Copilot’s Sign in, after the tokens Combwork keeps from Copilot (HI-2779): where that switch is. The path and the switch’s name are as Settings shows them (keep them as translated there); **…** marks bold text: keep the marks.

providers.copilot.updateAnyway.description: Provider Setup button: explicitly retry a failed WinGet Copilot update with --force, replacing the old package despite changed files.

providers.copilot.updateManual.defaultMessage: Update {provider} the way you installed it, then choose Check again.
providers.copilot.updateManual.description: Provider Setup, under a newer GitHub Copilot that Combwork can't update itself. {provider} is its name. Check again is the button in Provider Setup.

providers.copilot.updateModified.defaultMessage: WinGet could not remove the old Copilot package. Its installed files may have changed since WinGet installed them, often because Copilot updated itself. Update anyway asks WinGet to replace them with --force. Stop Copilot agents first.
providers.copilot.updateModified.description: Provider Setup after WinGet portable removal failed. The exit code can also mean other removal failures, so the cause is tentative. Update anyway is the adjacent button; keep WinGet, Copilot and --force unchanged.

providers.export.compacted.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): where the conversation was compacted. **…** is Markdown bold: keep the marks. {trigger} is how (auto or manual, in English); {before} and {after} its size in tokens (12.3k).

providers.export.error.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): over a tool call's failed result. **…** is Markdown bold: keep the marks.

providers.export.image.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): an image the user sent. *[…]* is Markdown: keep the marks.

providers.export.imageAt.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): an image the user sent, where the conversation had it. *[…]* is Markdown: keep the marks. {path} is its file.

providers.export.result.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): over a tool call's result. **…** is Markdown bold: keep the marks.

providers.export.subtitle.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): the line under its title. {provider} is the coding agent (Claude Code), {session} the session's id (`…` marks it: keep the marks), {project} the project.

providers.export.summary.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): the summary of a collapsed section holding a compaction's summary.

providers.export.thinking.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): the summary of a collapsed section holding the model's thinking.

providers.export.you.description: The Markdown export of a conversation (Sessions tab → Export): the heading over the user's messages.

providers.localLimits.context.defaultMessage: Context size {value, number} tokens ({from}){estimate, select, yes {: an estimate until Claude Code reports its window} other {}}
providers.localLimits.context.description: A line of the context tooltip of an agent on a local model (HI-2682): the context its launch gave Claude Code. {value} is a number of tokens; {from} where it was set ("Context size on Local", "env in …settings.json"). estimate yes: Claude Code hasn't reported its window yet. Keep the select keys.

providers.localLimits.inFile.description: Where a local model's limit came from, in brackets in its context tooltip (HI-2682): a Claude Code settings file's env block. {file} names the file. env is the block's name: keep it.

providers.localLimits.notUsed.defaultMessage: {why, select, alias {Context size not used: Claude Code reads {model} as one of its aliases} spelling {Context size not used: IDs with claude, [1m] or a date suffix aren’t supported for it} mapped {Context size not used: {file} maps {model} to a Claude model} unreadable {Context size not used: {file} couldn’t be read, so Combwork can’t tell whether it maps {model}} other {Context size not used: {model} isn’t one of {connection}’s models}}
providers.localLimits.notUsed.description: A line of the context tooltip of an agent on a local model (HI-2682): why its launch passed no context size. {model} is a model's id, {file} a settings file, {connection} the connection's name. Keep [1m] and the select keys.

providers.localLimits.ours.description: Where a local model's limit came from, in brackets in its context tooltip (HI-2682): the server connection's model fields, or their default. {connection} is the connection's name.

providers.localLimits.output.defaultMessage: Output budget {value, number} tokens ({from}){fallback, select, none {} other {: {fallback} wasn’t below the context, so the default was used}}
providers.localLimits.output.description: A line of the context tooltip of an agent on a local model (HI-2682): the output budget its launch gave Claude Code. {value} is a number of tokens; {from} where it was set; {fallback}: the budget it replaced, a number already formatted (none: leave that branch empty). Keep the select keys.

providers.localLimits.switched.defaultMessage: Started on {model} with these: they stay for the session, and Claude Code reports the window of the model it runs now.
providers.localLimits.switched.description: A line of the context tooltip of an agent on a local model (HI-2682): the session runs another model than it started on; the limits its launch passed still apply to the whole session. {model} is a model's id.

providers.memory.connection.description: In the Memory view: a connection's own instructions file (HI-1755), which the agents running on that connection read in every project. {file} is its name (CLAUDE.md), {name} the connection's name ("Personal").

providers.memory.user.description: In the Memory view: the user's own instructions file, which every project's agents read. {file} is its name (CLAUDE.md).

providers.opencode.adoptRefused.defaultMessage: Combwork can't take this OpenCode session over: {why, select, notRead {it hasn't been read from OpenCode yet} otherFolder {it ran in a folder that isn't this project's} otherMark {Combwork already has another session under its id} other {it isn't one of its account's sessions any more}}.
providers.opencode.adoptRefused.description: An error when adopting (taking over) a session from the Sessions tab: an OpenCode session made outside Combwork (in OpenCode's own window) couldn't be adopted. {why} picks the reason. OpenCode is a product's name.

providers.opencode.claudeAgentModel.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: {model} is a model of OpenCode's Claude Agent provider, which Combwork doesn't run through OpenCode. Run Claude Code as its own provider instead, or choose another model.
providers.opencode.claudeAgentModel.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't start (its pane): its model belongs to OpenCode's nested Claude Agent provider, which Combwork never allows. {provider} is OpenCode, {model} the model's id. Claude Agent and Claude Code are product names: keep them.

providers.opencode.connections.setUp.defaultMessage: Set Up runs `opencode auth login` on this account, so you can connect it to the model providers you use. Answer in the terminal; Combwork types nothing into it.
providers.opencode.connections.setUp.description: Settings → Accounts & Connections, above an OpenCode account's Set Up terminal: what Set Up is for. opencode auth login is a command: keep it. Set Up names a button.

providers.opencode.effortNeedsModel.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: the connection's effort is {effort}, which OpenCode sets as a variant of the model, and the connection names no model. Choose its model (a provider and model, such as ollama/qwen3:8b) or the default effort in Agent Settings.
providers.opencode.effortNeedsModel.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't start (its pane): an effort level is chosen, but OpenCode sets effort as a variant of a model and no model is chosen. {provider} is OpenCode, {effort} the effort as chosen (e.g. high). ollama/qwen3:8b is a model id: keep it. Agent Settings is a place in Combwork.

providers.opencode.effortNotListed.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: the connection's effort is {effort}, and OpenCode doesn't list {effort} as a variant of {model} on this account, so Combwork can't set it. Choose one of the model's efforts, or the default, in Agent Settings. If OpenCode's models couldn't be read just now, start the agent again.
providers.opencode.effortNotListed.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't start (its pane): the chosen effort level isn't one of the variants OpenCode lists for the chosen model on this account (or the list couldn't be read). {provider} is OpenCode, {effort} the effort as chosen (e.g. high), {model} the model's id. Agent Settings is a place in Combwork.

providers.opencode.historyBusy.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: Combwork's reader of OpenCode sessions didn't answer in time, so it couldn't take this session over from an earlier run. Start the agent again.
providers.opencode.historyBusy.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't start (its pane): Combwork's background reader of OpenCode session histories didn't confirm in time that it let go of the session's earlier run. {provider} is OpenCode.

providers.opencode.noModel.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: Combwork keeps OpenCode to the provider in the connection's model, and this connection names none, so OpenCode would choose one itself, perhaps one of its free cloud models. Choose the connection's model (a provider and model, such as ollama/qwen3:8b) in Agent Settings, or turn off "Keep OpenCode to the connection's own provider" in Settings → Advanced.
providers.opencode.noModel.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't start (its pane): Combwork only allows the provider of the connection's model, and no model (or no valid provider/model id) is set. {provider} is OpenCode. ollama/qwen3:8b is a model id: keep it. Agent Settings and Settings → Advanced are places in Combwork; the quoted text is an advanced setting's title: use that setting's translated title.

providers.opencode.noOwner.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: Combwork couldn't read its own process's identity, which the agent's private OpenCode server is tied to so that it ends with Combwork. Windows PowerShell may be blocked on this PC.
providers.opencode.noOwner.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't start (its pane): Combwork couldn't get the identity it ties the agent's server's lifetime to. {provider} is OpenCode. Windows PowerShell is a program's name: keep it.

providers.opencode.otherAccount.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't resume {session}: it is in another OpenCode account's data, not the account this agent runs on now. Start a new session, or move the agent back to that account.
providers.opencode.otherAccount.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't resume a session (its pane): each OpenCode account keeps its own sessions, and this one was made on another account. {provider} is OpenCode, {session} the session's id.

providers.opencode.protectedArg.defaultMessage: {provider} didn't start: the agent's extra arguments include {arg}, which Combwork sets itself for every OpenCode launch. Remove it from the agent's extra arguments (Agent Settings).
providers.opencode.protectedArg.description: Why an OpenCode agent didn't start (its pane): its extra command-line arguments include one Combwork controls (its server, its session, its mode). {provider} is OpenCode, {arg} the argument as typed. Agent Settings is a place in Combwork.

providers.opencode.v1Found.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {The opencode found is} other {The opencode copies found are}} not OpenCode 2: OpenCode 1 (opencode-ai), the archived opencode project or an editor’s copy. Combwork needs OpenCode 2: Install puts it in its own folder, and your other copy keeps working.
providers.opencode.v1Found.description: Provider Setup → OpenCode, when only copies Combwork doesn't support were found. opencode and opencode-ai are names: keep them; Install is a button.

providers.readiness.notInstalled.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Combwork didn't find the coding agent's CLI. {provider} is its name (Claude Code).

providers.readiness.signedOut.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: the coding agent's CLI has no sign-in. {provider} is its name.

providers.readiness.update.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: a newer version of the coding agent is out. {provider} is its name, {version} the version.

providers.readiness.updateStayed.defaultMessage: {provider} stayed on {version} after updating to {offered}: an organisation's policy may set its version or channel, or the update didn't take. Check again later, or update again.
providers.readiness.updateStayed.description: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: the coding agent was updated but is still on its old version (HI-2777). {provider} is its name, {version} the version it stayed on, {offered} the one offered. "Check again" and "update" name the buttons beside it.

providers.settings.hooksOff.defaultMessage: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} turns off all hooks (disableAllHooks). Combwork's hooks are how it knows what the agent is doing (its status, file locks, what it is told) and they carry its status line, so Combwork doesn't start an agent without them. Take disableAllHooks out of those settings, or remove the --settings from Extra arguments in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.hooksOff.description: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its settings turn Claude Code's hooks off. {source} is inline (settings written in the argument itself) or file; {file} is the file's path as the user wrote it. Keep --settings, disableAllHooks and the setting names as they are; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them.

providers.settings.noFile.description: Why a settings file can't be read, after "can't be read:" in another message: it doesn't exist.

providers.settings.noValue.defaultMessage: The last --settings in Extra arguments has no value. Give it a settings file or inline JSON (--settings '''<file or JSON>'''), or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.noValue.description: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its extra arguments end with --settings and nothing after it. Keep --settings as it is, and the straight quotes around <file or JSON>: each three apostrophes show one (ICU); the words file or JSON may be translated; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them.

providers.settings.notAFile.description: Why a settings file can't be read, after "can't be read:" in another message: the path is a folder or a device.

providers.settings.notJson.defaultMessage: The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments) isn't valid JSON ({why}). Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notJson.description: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its settings file isn't JSON. {file} is its path; {why} is the JSON parser's own words (English). Keep --settings and JSON as they are.

providers.settings.notList.defaultMessage: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} sets {key} to something other than a list, which stops Combwork's hooks reaching it. Make it a list ([ … ]) or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notList.description: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: a hook allowlist in its settings isn't a list. {key} is the setting's name. {source} is inline (settings written in the argument itself) or file; {file} is the file's path as the user wrote it. Keep --settings and the setting names as they are; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them. Keep [ … ] as it is.

providers.settings.notObject.defaultMessage: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} isn't a settings object ('{ … }'). Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notObject.description: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its settings aren't an object. {source} is inline (settings written in the argument itself) or file; {file} is the file's path as the user wrote it. Keep --settings and the setting names as they are; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them. Keep { … } as it is.

providers.settings.tooLarge.defaultMessage: it's over Claude Code's 2 MiB limit for settings files
providers.settings.tooLarge.description: Why a settings file can't be read, after "can't be read:" in another message: it is larger than Claude Code takes. Keep 2 MiB as it is.

providers.settings.unreadable.defaultMessage: The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments) can't be read: {why}. Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.unreadable.description: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: the settings file in its extra arguments can't be read. {file} is its path; {why} is the reason ("there is no such file", "it isn't a file", or the system's own words). Keep --settings as it is.

providers.transcript.aborted.description: A notice in a conversation, in the Sessions tab's transcript viewer and its Markdown export: the turn ended early, for no reason given.

providers.transcript.apiError.description: A notice in a conversation, in the Sessions tab's transcript viewer and its Markdown export: the coding agent's model API failed, with no message of its own.

providers.transcript.interrupted.description: A notice in a conversation, in the Sessions tab's transcript viewer and its Markdown export: the user stopped the agent's turn.

providers.transcript.opencodeForked.defaultMessage: Forked from another session: everything above was copied from it.
providers.transcript.opencodeForked.description: A notice in an OpenCode session's history (the Sessions tab's transcript viewer): this session is a fork (a copy made to continue separately) of another session; the messages above the notice came from that session, those below are this one's own.

providers.transcript.opencodeForkedSomew.defaultMessage: This session was forked from another one: some of it was copied from that session.
providers.transcript.opencodeForkedSomew.description: A notice at the start of an OpenCode session's history (the Sessions tab's transcript viewer): this session is a fork (a copy made to continue separately) of another session, and Combwork can't tell where the copied part ends.

providers.transcript.opencodeIncomplete.defaultMessage: Combwork couldn't read the end of this session from {provider}: {problem}. What's shown is what it had read before.
providers.transcript.opencodeIncomplete.description: A notice at the end of an OpenCode session's history (the Sessions tab's transcript viewer): Combwork's newest read of the session from OpenCode failed, so the end may be missing. {provider} is OpenCode; {problem} says why, one of the providers.transcript.opencodeProblem.* messages.

providers.transcript.opencodeProblem.exi.description: Why Combwork couldn't read an OpenCode session's end ({problem} in providers.transcript.opencodeIncomplete): the opencode command exited with an error. OpenCode is a product's name.

providers.transcript.opencodeProblem.par.defaultMessage: what OpenCode gave couldn't be read
providers.transcript.opencodeProblem.par.description: Why Combwork couldn't read an OpenCode session's end ({problem} in providers.transcript.opencodeIncomplete): OpenCode's answer wasn't in a shape Combwork knows. OpenCode is a product's name.

providers.transcript.opencodeProblem.siz.defaultMessage: the session is larger than Combwork reads
providers.transcript.opencodeProblem.siz.description: Why Combwork couldn't read an OpenCode session's end ({problem} in providers.transcript.opencodeIncomplete): it is over Combwork's size limit.

providers.transcript.opencodeProblem.tim.description: Why Combwork couldn't read an OpenCode session's end ({problem} in providers.transcript.opencodeIncomplete): OpenCode didn't answer in time.

providers.transcript.opencodeRevertStage.defaultMessage: OpenCode has this message and everything after it marked to be undone.
providers.transcript.opencodeRevertStage.description: A notice in an OpenCode session's history (the Sessions tab's transcript viewer), placed before a message: the user chose to undo (revert) the conversation from here in OpenCode, and hasn't confirmed it yet, so what follows is still shown. OpenCode is a product's name.

providers.transcript.resumed.description: A notice in a conversation, in the Sessions tab's transcript viewer and its Markdown export: the conversation was resumed here (GitHub Copilot).

providers.transcript.turnEnded.description: A notice in a conversation, in the Sessions tab's transcript viewer and its Markdown export: the turn ended early. {reason} is the coding agent's own word for why (timeout), in English.

providers.unknown.defaultMessage: Unknown provider "{provider}". It may need a newer version of Combwork.
providers.unknown.description: An agent or a setting names a coding-agent CLI this version of Combwork doesn't know, as when a newer Combwork wrote it. {provider} is the id.
